newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Hong Leong denies bank merger rumours.
newsitem.headline: Hong Leong denies bank merger rumours.

text.p: Hong Leong Bank Bhd said on Monday that it is not involved in a merger with Ban Hin Lee Bank Bhd.

James Lim, senior group managing director of Hong Leong Bank, was responding to reporters' questions about the rumoured merger. "I have no knowledge of these reports," he said. "At this time, it's not happening."
Lim added, "We have not written to Bank Negara to apply for any such merger."

On Friday, Ban Hin Lee also said it was unaware of any plans for a rumoured merger with Hong Leong Bank. Last week, talk surfaced in the market that property firm Advance Synergy Bhd may be seeking to buy a stake in Ban Hin Lee, and later sell or merge it with Hong Leong Bank.
Five percent of Advance Synergy's equity is owned by Hong Leong group.

In a further comment about mergers, Lim said, "Whether we merge or buy another bank depends on whether the opportunity exists. If the price is right, we will. But we will not pay an exorbitant price to buy another institution."
Speculation about possible bank mergers has circulated following the 2.16 billion ringgit merger between DCB Holdings Bhd and Kwong Yik Bank Bhd last month.
